identity: An Arabic news-wire / broadcast-news dispatch (doctrine register §Q), almost certainly translated from French agency copy: a France24/RFI-shaped report that the EU will ease sanctions on Iran, built around statements by French foreign minister Laurent Fabius to Europe 1 radio, followed by a Saudi reaction to the Geneva accord. Layout: a 7-token headline, then four body paragraphs delimited by <NL> at 7, 77, 135, 162. 217 tokens total. Hallmarks of the register are all present: a dateline adverb (اليوم الإثنين), a full name+title+outlet attribution block, a P5+1 country list, a date with a Gregorian gloss (كانون الأول ديسمبر), scare-quoted ministerial phrases, and a closing official-statement quotation.
law: The unit is the printed full stop of wire copy, and in this register the paragraph is close to the sentence (§Q3): four of my nine segments are exactly one paragraph. Within a paragraph a sentence ends at one place only — where a NEW REPORTING ACT begins, i.e. a fresh finite speech verb with its own complement and its own attributed content (وقال أيضا / كما أكد / كما قال / كما لمح). Nothing below that level cuts. Specifically welded here: a comma-list of country names (LAW 3), a number group (5 1, أوروبا 1 — A2), a date and its gloss (A2b), a speech verb and the whole of its quotation however many clauses the quotation contains (G1), a prose colon before an attributed statement (A4), a trailing على الرغم من / لأن / إذا / طالما-apodosis adjunct (LAW 4), حيث (B2 as revised), and ولكن (B4 as revised). My reason for every cut names a mark in the source, never a connective — per checklist item 2, and per the batch-2 lesson that cost me 354 false cuts.
reasoning: CALIBRATION FIRST (LAW 6). Step zero of my checklist: not scripture (no verse cues, no Van Dyck vocabulary), not a quiz/worksheet, not dialogue or balloons — so the unit is the printed full stop, target 25-40 tokens (§Q). The five free boundaries are 6, 76, 134, 161 (each immediately before a <NL>) and 216 (final token); an <NL> never carries one itself. That leaves paragraph interiors, and I made only four judgment cuts in 217 tokens — a deliberately conservative posture given my logged 22:1 over-cutting swing in batch 2 and LAW 0-double-prime (coin flip => weld). Resulting units: 7 / 45 / 24 / 13 / 11 / 20 / 13 / 26 / 54. || SITE @52/53, وألمانيا | وقال أيضا — CUT (hi). The preceding stretch 8-52 is a single closed reported-speech frame: أعلن + full أن-complement, running out into the P5+1 apposition. Three reasons that are marks, not connectives. (a) أيضا lexically presupposes a completed prior assertion — you cannot say 'and he ALSO said X' as a continuation of the very clause it adds to. (b) The mode shifts from indirect (أن + clause) to direct quotation. (c) 69 tokens is longer than any unit in my register table outside an MCQ stem, whereas 45 + 24 sits squarely in §Q. I checked the LAW 5 off-by-one: the alternative joint at 54 (وقال أيضا | إيران ملتزمة) is the G1/M2-forbidden split of a speech verb from its quote, so 52 is the only candidate. || SITE @62/63, نووية | هذا أمر واضح كل الوضوح — WELD. This was my closest call. The pull to cut is real: هذا أمر واضح كل الوضوح is asyndetic and syntactically independent, and the source surely printed a stop or comma between the two halves of Fabius's remark. But G1 is the most-confirmed rule in my file (a whole quoted utterance is ONE segment with its speech verb, however many clauses it contains — confirmed in five registers in batch 2), and LAW 3 as revised tells me that when I cannot be sure each element was a complete PRINTED sentence I weld, because in batch 2 the weld was right every single time. The batch-1 cases that did cut (أنا أقوى الأقوياء || أنا عظيم العظماء) were exclamatory sentences in a 5-10-token graded-reader register, which §E now explicitly forbids me to export. Weld. || SITE @67/68, كل الوضوح | ولكنه لم يكشف — WELD, and I want to record that I argued myself OUT of a cut here. My first pass reasoned: the quote closes, the journalist resumes, ولكنه is third-person while the quoted content is Fabius's own voice, therefore a person-deixis flip that is impossible inside one sentence — cut. That argument is wrong. The quotation is the direct object of وقال, so the -ه of ولكنه resumes the subject of قال, not anyone inside the quote; وقال أيضا 'X' ولكنه لم يكشف عن... is a perfectly well-formed single sentence and is in fact a stock wire construction ('he said X but did not specify Y'). With the deixis argument gone, B4 as revised governs: a ولكن-clause welds by default at any length and cuts only where a full stop precedes it — and I have four batch-2 false cuts on precisely this ولكنه/لكنه form. Weld, giving a clean 24-token §Q unit. || THE كما SERIES, paragraph 3 — my main deviation from a standing doctrine entry, argued explicitly. Checklist item 2 lists كما among connectives that are 'not a reason' to cut, on the strength of one batch-2 false cut, doc_1c49614cd6bc @219, gold ...عندما كان المسلمون يخرجون كما حصل في غزوة أحد.... But that is COMPARATIVE كما ('as happened at Uhud'), a subordinating particle inside a clause. What paragraph 3 contains four times is ADDITIVE sentence-initial كما + finite speech verb ('he further affirmed', 'he also said'), which is a different construction. Three independent grounds. (1) The document proves the construction is sentence-initial in its own hand: the paragraph OPENS with كما أكد immediately after the <NL> at 77, a position that is a boundary by law. (2) LAW 3's surviving discriminator asks 'was each element a complete printed sentence, or an item inside one?' — each of the four is an independent main clause with its own finite reporting verb and its own أن/إن complement, with no coordination, no subordination and no connective linking them; that is the opposite of the false-cut cases (والعقل ليس..., فإنه يجدر..., حيث تقول, إذ نشاهد), every one of which was syntactically DEPENDENT on what preceded. (3) 57 tokens juxtaposing four bare reporting verbs cannot be one printed sentence in edited Arabic. Note also that the choice is all-or-nothing: since the construction is identical at all four instances, welding some and cutting others would be incoherent, so the real contest is 13/11/20/13 versus a single 57, and 57 is impossible. I therefore cut at 90 (أسابيع, before كما قال), 101 (للتراجع, before كما قال) and 121 (نهائية, before كما لمح). Confidence is hi only at 101, where the argument is structural rather than stylistic: كما قال is immediately followed at 102 by a second كما قال, and two identical reporting frames cannot sit inside one sentence. 90 and 121 inherit from the parallelism and get med. I flag the whole class as a tension for my next doctrine pass: additive كما may need splitting out from comparative كما as its own entry. || Sites inside paragraph 3 that WELD: @114/115 (تسوية | لم يتم التوصل) is the protasis/apodosis joint of the طالما conditional and sits inside the quotation attributed to قال — a comma at most (LAW 0-prime, G1). || PARAGRAPH 4 = ONE SEGMENT, 26 tokens, no internal cut. @151/152 (إيران | قال) is a fronted circumstantial adjunct وفي معرض رد الوزير... meeting its main verb — a sentence-opening adverbial, never a boundary. @152/153 never separates قال from its quote (G1). @156/157 (لا | لأن لا أحد سيتفهم ذلك): I considered H3, which makes a bare interjection its own segment and which supplied 5 of my 16 batch-2 misses — but لا here is not a standalone conversational turn, it is the first word of a quoted reply that continues into its own reason clause, and LAW 4 puts a trailing لأن with its main clause (doc_4f0612ce35d1 @271). The length is honestly accounted for: a fronted adjunct, a main clause, a concessive, a relative clause and a 22-token embedded quotation. || LOW-LEVEL WELDS CHECKED AND CONFIRMED: 5 1 at 42-43 is the P5+1 number group (A2 — never cut inside digits, the exact shape of my doc_2fabc1ccf342 @90 false cut on 0.2%); أوروبا 1 at 17-18 is a station name containing a digit; كانون الأول ديسمبر at 29-31 is a date plus its Gregorian gloss (A2b); and the seven-country run at 46-52 is a comma-list, welded entire, the same phenomenon as the thirteen-name run at doc_0de3fe1bcb6c @325-@350 that cost me twelve consecutive false cuts.
